newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum market remains subdued-Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum market remains subdued-Grainco.

text.p: The sorghum market in southern Queensland remains relatively subdued, Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd Trading manager Rob Brealey said.
While there has been some grower selling and trade and consumer buying domestically, the tonnages remain relatively small with most people looking to the skies for price direction.

"The sorghum market in southern Queensland remains relatively subdued, however with the new financial year upon us, it will be interesting to see whether current values tempt grower selling," he said in his weekly market report.

With the continuing negative news coming out of the export market, growers in Central Queensland remain extremely reluctant sellers at current levels, most waiting and hoping for a problem which will translate to higher futures in the short to medium term, Brealey said.
Early barley yields in Europe have been better than expected which has given the international price a bearish tone.

Recent Middle East tenders were executed at the equivalent US$126 a tonne fob Australian port for September/October delivery which was lower than expected due to harvest pressure. Despite recent rainfalls in southern areas of Australia, further
widespread rain is needed in parts of New South Wales (NSW) to complete barley planting.
In Queensland, falls of 25-50 mm are urgently needed across the southern and central downs in the next three weeks to achieve the planting estimates of 150,000 hectares.

Old crop feed barley values finished the week unchanged at around A$175/mt delivered Brisbane for June-July, reflecting a premium over export values which have moved lower at around US$135 a tonne on an fob basis.
New crop values ended the week at around A$155 a tonne for November-December and A$160 for strict October delivery.
New crop malting barley values remain generally supported in the international market and finished last week at A$185 a tonne.

Continuing strong export demand for cottonseed from the Japanese and Korean markets is being seen for prompt shipment right through until new crop, however export price ideas are still well below current levels being six to eight weeks ago.
The sale of 30,000 tonnes to bulk export destinations combined with increased domestic feeding interest is slowly changing Asian buyers minds, Brealey said.
Cash prices are trading at around A$155 a tonne Downs gin to the grower with very little selling interest.
In central Queensland prices have firmed to A$150 ex gin for ginning period delivery to domestic consumers.

Sowing of pulses continues in much of Queensland and northern New South Wales where conditions allow. In drier areas, many farmers are still intending to plant some acreage to pulses, however they are awaiting further rains.
Price indications for the new crop continue at around the A$310 a tonne delivered port basis for Queensland chickpeas and faba beans at around A$250 a tonne port for the new crop.
Sunflower prices remained steady and finished the week at A$327 delivered Brisbane for the June - July and A$337 delivered Newcastle for June-July delivery.
Central Queensland sunflower prices also finished higher at A$282 - A$287 delivered central Queensland depot (depending on location) for the June-July delivery period.
New crop soybean prices moved lower at A$405 delivered Brisbane for June.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2-9372-1800
